result.summary: Removes the `-persistmempoolv1` command-line option and stops support for writing legacy non-XORed `mempool.dat` files on shutdown or via `savemempool`. Reading existing v1 mempool files remains supported to allow seamless upgrades from old versions. The PR also updates `mempool_compatibility.py` to test against v31.0 and adds a test case for importing malformed mempool dumps.
result.problem: The `-persistmempoolv1` option was introduced as a temporary fallback to allow users to downgrade to v26.x or earlier, which could not read XOR-obfuscated `mempool.dat` files. Because v26 and earlier releases have reached end-of-life, the fallback option is unnecessary technical debt.
evidence: PR description: "-persistmempoolv1 was added in #28207 as a temporary option to allow downgrading to v26 and earlier, which can't read the XOR'ed mempool.dat. v26 has now been EOL for a while... docs have always stated that this was a 'temporary option that will be removed in the future'."
Existing help text in src/init.cpp explicitly noted: "This temporary option will be removed in the future."
result.changed_since_previous: Updated `mempool_compatibility.py` to use v31.0 as the old node release instead of v28.2, and added a functional test verifying that `importmempool` rejects a malformed `mempool.dat` file.
result.card: This pull request removes the `-persistmempoolv1` configuration option, dropping the ability to write legacy non-XORed `mempool.dat` files on node shutdown or during `savemempool`. It removes temporary compatibility code introduced in Bitcoin Core v27 now that v26 and earlier versions are end-of-life. Node operators can still read legacy v1 files when upgrading from older releases. The only affected users are those attempting to downgrade to unsupported versions older than v27.

risk.why: A mistake could break mempool serialization on shutdown, which would cause nodes to start with empty mempools but would not cause consensus or state corruption.
